request.spec:
The sheet has a pending SLA (settings, days, not dated; SETTING_CHANGED key=pending-sla
value=<days>; blank means none). A PENDING claim whose pending day (the sheet's today when it went
to PENDING, the latest time) plus the SLA is before the sheet's today shows pending-late yes; the
summary counts such claims.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The sheet has a pending SLA (settings, days, not dated; SETTING_CHANGED key=pending-sla
value=<days>; blank means none). A PENDING claim whose pending day (the sheet's today when it went
to PENDING, the latest time) plus the SLA is before the sheet's today shows pending-late yes; the
summary counts such claims.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text: The background job I'd set up to wait for the e2e run hit its time limit and was stopped. Its check for a running `bin/e2e` was probably matching its own command line, so it never saw the run end. That doesn't affect the result: the e2e run had already finished and all 4 tests passed, as reported above. Nothing else is running and nothing needs to be redone.
